blockMcqs.question: What single goal do software design principles ultimately serve?
options: Making code run faster at runtime
Keeping the cost of change low
Reducing the total lines of code
Maximizing reuse across projects
blockMcqs.explanation: Maintenance dominates lifetime cost, so design optimizes for cheap future change.

blockMcqs.question: What is the difference between coupling and cohesion?
options: Coupling is within a module; cohesion is between modules
Both measure dependency between modules
Coupling is between modules; cohesion is focus within one
Both measure how many lines a module has
blockMcqs.explanation: You want dependency low across modules and focus high inside each one.

blockMcqs.question: Which SOLID principle says add behavior without editing working code?
options: Single Responsibility
Open/Closed
Liskov Substitution
Dependency Inversion
blockMcqs.explanation: Polymorphism lets new implementations extend behavior without touching tested code.

blockMcqs.question: What is the real test for a Single Responsibility violation?
options: The class has more than one public method
The class spans more than one file
More than one stakeholder drives changes to it
The class has more than one field
blockMcqs.explanation: Responsibility is about reasons to change, not method or line counts.

blockMcqs.question: Why does `Square extends Rectangle` violate Liskov substitution?
options: Squares cannot be drawn on screen
It surprises callers who set width independently of height
Rectangle is an abstract class
Squares need more memory than rectangles
blockMcqs.explanation: A subtype must honor the parent's contract; this one breaks caller assumptions.

blockMcqs.question: DRY is fundamentally about not duplicating what?
options: Identical lines of text
Business knowledge
Class names
Test cases
blockMcqs.explanation: Each business rule should live in one place; identical-looking text may differ in meaning.

blockMcqs.question: Why prefer composition over inheritance for varying behavior?
options: Inheritance is slower at runtime
Composition uses less memory
Inheritance creates fragile base-class coupling
Composition needs fewer total classes
blockMcqs.explanation: Subclasses lean on the base's internals, so a base change silently breaks them.

blockMcqs.question: Injecting a `Store` and `Notifier` into `OrderService` mainly serves which?
options: Dependency Inversion, enabling testable swappable parts
Single Responsibility for the notifier only
Liskov Substitution across stores
Interface Segregation of the order model
blockMcqs.explanation: Depending on abstractions lets fakes plug in and new channels add without edits.
